title: The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Manmohan Singh Jaiswal on 14 October, 2013
doc:
The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Manmohan Singh Jaiswal on 14 October, 2013

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION UTTARAKHAND
                         DEHRADUN

                    FIRST APPEAL NO. 92 / 2012

The New India Assurance Company Limited
through Deputy Manager
Regional Office, Astley Hall
Dehradun
                                       ......Appellant / Opposite Party

                                Versus

Sh. Manmohan Singh Jaiswal S/o Sardar Amar Singh
R/o Ganesh Co-operative Housing Society
Room No. 17/18, Landour Bazar
Mussoorie
                                        ......Respondent / Complainant

Smt. Anjali Gusain, Learned Counsel for the Appellant
Sh. Nusrat Ali Ansari, Learned Counsel for Respondent

Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice B.C. Kandpal, President
       Mr. C.C. Pant,                    Member

Dated: 14/10/2013

                               ORDER

(Per: Justice B.C. Kandpal, President):

This is insurer's appeal under Section 15 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 against the order dated 21.05.2012 passed by the District Forum, Dehradun in consumer complaint No. 121 of 2011. By the order impugned, the District Forum has allowed the consumer complaint and directed the appellant - opposite party to pay compensation of Rs. 2,67,575/- to the respondent - complainant; Rs. 10,000/- towards mental agony and Rs. 10,000/- towards litigation expenses. The above amount was directed to be paid within a period of one month from the date of the order, failing which the same was directed to carry interest @9% p.a. from the date of filing of the consumer complaint till payment.
2

2. Briefly stated, the facts of the case as mentioned in the consumer complaint, are that the complainant was the registered owner of vehicle No. UA07-J-7009 (Toyota Qualis). The said vehicle was insured with the appellant - The New India Assurance Company Limited for the period from 25.01.2011 to 24.01.2012. It is alleged that the complainant was granted tourist permit No. 473/STA/AI for the said vehicle by State / Regional Transport Authority, Uttaranchal, which was valid for the period from 19.02.2010 to 18.02.2015. As per the said permit, the complainant was authorised to ply the said vehicle in the State of Uttarakhand and the States mentioned in the authorisation certificate. It is also alleged that on 04.02.2011, the complainant went to New Delhi to meet his son by the insured vehicle. The complainant parked the insured vehicle outside the house of his son and went to the 2nd floor of the house. In the night at 11:45 p.m., when the complainant went out to see the vehicle, he found that the vehicle had been stolen. The complainant immediately lodged the FIR with P.S. Vikaspuri, New Delhi and also gave intimation of theft of the insured vehicle to the insurance company. The police submitted the Final Report on 20.03.2011, stating therein that inspite of efforts, the stolen property (insured vehicle) could not be recovered. The complainant lodged the claim with the insurance company, but the insurance company repudiated the claim on the ground that on the date of incident of theft, the complainant was not having a valid permit. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the insurance company, the complainant filed a consumer complaint before the District Forum, Dehradun.

3. The insurance company filed written statement before the District Forum and pleaded that the complainant was not having a valid permit to ply the insured vehicle within the territory of State of 3 Delhi and that no deficiency in service was made by the insurance company in repudiating the claim on the said ground.

4. The District Forum, on an appreciation of the material on record, allowed the consumer complaint vide impugned order dated 21.05.2012 in the above terms. Aggrieved by the said order, the insurance company has filed this appeal.

5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have also perused the record.

6. The insurance company has taken the defence that on investigation of the matter, it was found that the insured vehicle was not having any permit for plying the same in Delhi and since the vehicle was stolen at Delhi and hence the claim was not payable and was rightly repudiated on the said ground vide repudiation letter dated 23.05.2011 (Paper No. 22).

7. After perusal of the material available on record, it appears that in the tourist permit (Paper No. 21) issued in favour of the complainant, it has specifically been mentioned at Sl. No. 5 that the permit is valid for "all Uttarakhand and State mentioned in Authorisation Certificate". The Authorisation for Tourist Permit issued in favour of the complainant by the Secretary, State Transport Authority, Uttarakhand is on record (Paper No. 20). The said authorisation was valid throughout the territory of India and as per the said authorisation certificate, before entering into another State, the complainant had to deposit the tax or fees, whichever is applicable, with the nearest check post or Transport Department. Hence, the complainant was authorised to ply the insured vehicle throughout the territory of India. Before entering into the State of Delhi, the 4 complainant had deposited the toll tax at Gazipur Toll Plaza and the receipt in that respect dated 04.02.2011 issued by Municipal Corporation of Delhi is on record (Paper No. 23). Thus, as per the condition stipulated in the authorisation certificate, the complainant had deposited the toll tax before entering in the State of Delhi. It may also be mentioned here that the incident of theft also took place in the night of 04.02.2011. Hence, in the above circumstances, it can not be said that the complainant was not authorised to ply the subject vehicle within the vicinity of State of Delhi and hence has committed breach of the terms and conditions of the policy and the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. As such, the repudiation of the claim by the insurance company can not be said to be justified and the insurance company has definitely made deficiency in service by repudiating the claim of the complainant and the District Forum was perfectly justified in allowing the consumer complaint.

8. So far as the quantum is concerned, the vehicle was insured for sum of Rs. 2,62,575/- for the period from 25.01.2011 to 24.01.2012, which is evident from the insurance policy on record (Paper No. 18). The complainant has also averred in para 3 of his consumer complaint that the vehicle was insured for sum of Rs. 2,62,575/-. The incident of theft took place in the night of 04.02.2011, i.e., within a period of 10 days of the date of insurance of the vehicle. Therefore, there is no question of any depreciation on account of use of the vehicle for such a short period of less than 10 days. The District Forum has awarded a sum of Rs. 2,67,575/-. We are unable to understand as to from where the District Forum arrived at the said figure. Since the vehicle was insured for sum of Rs. 2,62,575/- and hence the complainant is entitled to the said amount. So far as the interest awarded @9% p.a. is concerned, we are of the view that the same is on the higher side and in our considered view, interest @7% p.a. would be just and proper.

5

Since the complainant has been awarded interest, there is no question of separate compensation for mental agony and hence the award of Rs. 10,000/- passed by the District Forum towards mental agony, is liable to be set aside. We are further of the view that the litigation expenses of Rs. 10,000/- awarded by the District Forum are also on the higher side and the same need to be reduced to Rs. 5,000/-. This way, the appeal succeeds partly and is to be allowed accordingly and the order impugned is liable to be modified as such.

9. For the reasons aforesaid, appeal is partly allowed. Order impugned dated 21.05.2012 of the District Forum is modified and the appellant - insurance company is directed to pay sum of Rs. 2,62,575/- to the respondent - complainant together with interest @7% p.a. from the date of filing of the consumer complaint till payment and Rs. 5,000/- towards litigation expenses. However, costs of the appeal made easy. 

            (C.C. PANT)                (JUSTICE B.C. KANDPAL)
K
